metadata.description: Verified corpus of public domain and academic open-access Gojri literature and language specimens.
metadata.attribution: Compiled from Grierson (1908), Sharma (1982), and Losey (2002).

books.title: Linguistic Survey of India: Specimens of Gujari / Gojri
books.author: Sir George Abraham Grierson
books.description: Specimens of the Gujari language collected from Poonch (J&K) and Hazara during the Linguistic Survey of India (Vol. IX, Part IV). Contains the classical interlinear Parable of the Prodigal Son.

pages.section_title: Parable of the Prodigal Son - Opening (Poonch specimen)
pages.text_perso_arabic: ہک آدمی کا دو پتر تھیا۔ انھاں ماں کن چھوٹو اپنے باپو نا بولیو کہ باپو مال رو جیہڑو حصہ مھارا آوے سو منے دے۔
pages.text_devanagari: हिक आदमी का दो पुत्तर थिया। इन्हाँ माँ कन छोटो अपने बापू ना बोल्यो कि बापू माल रो जेहड़ो हिस्सा म्हारो आवे सो मने दे।
pages.text_roman: Hik ādmī kā do puttar thiyā. Inhā̃ mā̃ kan chhoṭo apne bāpū nā bolyo ki bāpū māl ro jehṛo hisso mhāro āve so mane de.
pages.translation_en: A certain man had two sons. And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me.
pages.notes: Recorded in Poonch, Western Jammu & Kashmir; exhibits typical Gojri genitive 'ro/ri' and agentive/dative 'nā'.

pages.section_title: Parable of the Prodigal Son - Departure and Want
pages.text_perso_arabic: تھوڑیاں دہاڑیاں پچھے چھوٹو پتر سبھ کجھ کٹھو کر کے پردیس ٹر گیو۔ اوتھے اپنے مال نا بدمعاشی ما اڑائی چھڈیو۔
pages.text_devanagari: थोड़ियां दिहाड़ियां पीछे छोटो पुत्तर सभ कुझ कठो कर के परदेस टुर ग्यो। ओथे अपने माल ना बदमाशी मा उड़ाई छड्यो।
pages.text_roman: Thoṛyā̃ dihāṛyā̃ pachhe chhoṭo puttar sabh kujh kaṭho kar ke pardes ṭur gyo. Othe apne māl nā badmāshī mā uṛāī chhaḍyo.
pages.translation_en: And not many days after, the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
pages.notes: Past participle 'ṭur gyo' (went away) and compound verb 'uṛāī chhaḍyo' (squandered away).

pages.section_title: Parable of the Prodigal Son - Repentance and Return
pages.text_perso_arabic: جد ہوش ما آیو تا بولیو کہ مھارے باپو کے کنے مزدوراں نا رج کھانو ملتو ہے تے ہوں اتھے بھکھو مروں چھوں۔
pages.text_devanagari: जद होश मा आयो ता बोल्यो कि म्हारे बापू के कने मज़दूराँ ना रज खानो मिलतो है ते हूँ इथे भुक्खो मरों छूँ।
pages.text_roman: Jad hosh mā āyo tā bolyo ki mhāre bāpū ke kane mazdūrā̃ nā raj khāno milto hai te hū̃ ithe bhukkho marõ chhū̃.
pages.translation_en: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
pages.notes: Contains 1st person 'hū̃' and auxiliary form 'chhū̃' (I am).

books.title: Gojri Grammar: Narrative and Folk Texts
books.author: J. C. Sharma
books.publisher: Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL), Mysore
books.description: Authentic narrative texts, folktales, and pastoral discourse recorded during CIIL linguistic field research in Jammu & Kashmir.

pages.section_title: The Shepherd and the Flock (چرواہو تے اِجّڑ / Charwāho te Ijjaṛ)
pages.text_perso_arabic: اک چرواہو روز پہاڑاں ما اپنے اِجّڑ نا چراوݨ جاؤتو سی۔ اوہ ساریاں بھیڈاں بکریاں نا پیار نال سَمبھالو سی۔
pages.text_devanagari: इक चरवाहो रोज़ पहाड़ाँ मा अपने इज्जड़ ना चरावण जावतो सी। ओह सारियाँ भीडाँ बकरियाँ ना प्यार नाल सम्भालो सी।
pages.text_roman: Ik charwāho roz pahāṛā̃ mā apne ijjaṛ nā charāvaṇ jāvto sī. Oh sāriyā̃ bhīḍā̃ bakriyā̃ nā pyār nāl sambhālo sī.
pages.translation_en: A shepherd used to go to the mountains daily to graze his flock. He took care of all the sheep and goats with affection.
pages.notes: Narrative past habitual: 'jāvto sī' (used to go); pastoral keyword 'ijjaṛ' (flock of sheep/goats).

pages.section_title: High Mountain Pastures (دھار تے ڈہوکاں / Dhār te Ḍhokā̃)
pages.text_perso_arabic: گرمی دے مہینیاں ما گجر اپݨا مال ڈنگر لے کے اُچی دھاراں تے ڈہوکاں وال ٹر جاؤندے نیں۔ برف پگھلݨ تے ہری گھاہ پھٹدی ہے۔
pages.text_devanagari: गर्मी दे महीन्याँ मा गुज्जर अपणा माल डंगर ले के उस धाराँ ते ढोकाँ वाल टुर जावन्दे ने। बर्फ पिघलण ते हरी घाह फुटदी है।
pages.text_roman: Garmī de mahīnyā̃ mā Gujjar apṇā māl-ḍangar le ke uchī dhārā̃ te ḍhokā̃ vāl ṭur jāvande ne. Baraf pighlaṇ te harī ghāh phuṭdī hai.
pages.translation_en: During summer months, Gujjars travel toward high mountain ridges (dhār) and temporary highland settlements (ḍhok) with their cattle. When snow melts, fresh green grass sprouts.
pages.notes: Transhumance culture documentation: 'dhār' (mountain ridge) and 'ḍhok' (highland pastoral summer cottage).

books.title: Writing Gojri: Literacy, Proverbs, and Dialogue Specimens
books.author: Wayne E. Losey
books.publisher: SIL International & University of North Dakota
books.description: Sociolinguistic and orthographic texts documenting communicative interaction, community proverbs, and literacy materials.

pages.text_perso_arabic: سلام علیکم! تساں رو کی حال چال ہے؟ گھر بار سبھ خیریت نال ہے؟ آؤ اندر لنگھ آؤ، چاہ پیؤ۔
pages.text_devanagari: सलाम अलैकुम! तुसाँ रो की हाल चाल है? घर बार सभ ख़ैरियत नाल है? आवो अन्दर लंघ आवो, चाह पियो।
pages.text_roman: Salām 'alaikum! Tusā̃ ro kī hāl chāl hai? Ghar bār sabh khairiyat nāl hai? Āo andar langh āo, chāh pīo.
pages.translation_en: Peace be upon you! How are you doing? Is everything well at home? Please come inside, have some tea.
pages.notes: Typical polite register: 2nd plural genitive 'tusā̃ ro' and imperative 'langh āo' (step inside).

pages.section_title: Wisdom of the Elders (بزرگاں ری نصیحت / Buzurgā̃ rī Nasīhat)
pages.text_perso_arabic: جے تو محنت کریگا تاں اللہ برکت دیسی۔ جیہڑو بوئیگا سوئی وڈھیگا، ایہہ جگ ری ریت ہے۔
pages.text_devanagari: जे तू मेहनत करेगा ताँ अल्लाह बरकत देसी। जेहड़ो बोवेगा सोई वढेगा, एह जग री रीत है।
pages.text_roman: Je tū mehnat karegā tā̃ Allāh barkat desī. Jehṛo boegā soī vaḍhegā, eh jag rī rīt hai.
pages.translation_en: If you work hard, God will grant blessing. As you sow, so shall you reap; such is the way of the world.
pages.notes: Correlative structure: 'jehṛo ... soī' (whoever ... he); synthetic future 'desī' (will give).
